transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, what brings me in is that... my head just feels really cloudy lately. I'll be sitting there staring at a board packet or an email from a vendor, and I just can't seem to make a decision. Even simple things that I used to handle fast, I just... I can't think through them right now.
How long have you been noticing this trouble concentrating and making decisions?

It's been about two weeks. It started right around the time my husband retired and was suddenly home all day. I just noticed this... sharper change in my energy and my confidence, and then it turned into this low, cloudy feeling I have right now.
Have you ever had a period like this before, with low mood and trouble concentrating lasting two weeks or more, even before this recent situation with your husband?

Yeah, I have. These kind of depressed stretches... they've actually been coming back on and off for about a year now, I'd say. But this latest one just feels a lot more tied to what happened after my husband stopped working.

Over this past year, between these depressed stretches, have there been times when your mood returned completely to normal for weeks at a time, or has it felt more like a low mood that's been present most of the time?

Well, I guess... between those stretches, my mood does go back to normal. Yeah, I'd say I have weeks where I feel completely fine, just like my usual self. It hasn't been a constant low mood the whole year, just... coming and going.
During this past two weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

Yes, I have. I just... I haven't wanted to go to my dance class at all. I usually like to go look at the little galleries around town, but I haven't done that either. I haven't even wanted to cook the Sunday food for my family... and those are the things that usually make me feel like myself. I just don't have the interest right now.
Over these past two weeks, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
No, not really. I mean... my sleep has been pretty normal, actually. I go to bed and wake up around the same time I always do. I haven't had any trouble falling asleep or sleeping too much.

You mentioned feeling a 'sharper' rise in energy and confidence right before this low mood started—can you tell me more about that period? For example, did you feel unusually energetic, need less sleep than usual, or feel more talkative or confident than normal?

Yes, I did feel more talkative and confident. Actually, there were days when I felt almost... too bright and bold. Like at the association meetings, I would find myself just talking right over people to get my point across. But it wasn't just feeling good, it also made me a bit short-tempered. I would come home and just snap at my husband over some small thing that normally wouldn't bother me at all. It was just a very sharp kind of energy.
How many days in a row did that period of feeling unusually energetic, talkative, and short-tempered last before your mood shifted into feeling low?
I'm not exactly sure how many days in a row it was. I didn't really count them. I just know it went on for a little while before I started feeling so down.
Thinking back, do you think that period of feeling unusually energetic and talkative lasted at least 4 days in a row before your mood shifted to feeling low?
I really can't say for sure. I didn't keep track of the days... it just felt like a stretch of time where I was like that, before the crash happened. I don't know if it was exactly four days or not.
Did anyone close to you, like your husband or coworkers, comment that you seemed unusually energetic or different for several days in a row during that time?

No, my husband didn't say anything about it lasting for days. He just told me I was being snappy and difficult to be around. And the people at work or the association... well, they didn't really say anything to my face about me being different. I just know I was talking a lot more than usual. But nobody pointed it out as being some kind of streak or anything.

Can you recall any specific days or events—like particular meetings, appointments, or activities—that happened during that energetic stretch, which might help us figure out about how many days it lasted?

I'm trying to think... but no, not really. I mean, my work with the association is mostly just the same routine every day—answering phone calls, dealing with property issues. Nothing really stands out like a big meeting or a specific appointment that would help me pin down the exact days. It all just kind of blends together when I try to look back on it. I just can't give you an exact number.
During that stretch when you felt unusually energetic and talkative, did you notice needing less sleep than usual but still feeling rested, or was your sleep about the same as normal?

I don't really remember my sleep being any different. I usually sleep about the same amount every night, and I don't think that changed when I was feeling more energetic. I definitely didn't feel like I could just run on a few hours of sleep or anything like that.
Thinking about that energetic, talkative stretch before you crashed—did it feel like it lasted more like a whole week, or was it really just a day or two?

I really don't know for sure. Like I said, it all just kind of blends together. I don't think it was a whole week, but I can't honestly say if it was just a day or two either. I just know it happened before I crashed, but the exact amount of time... I just don't have a clear memory of that.

During that energetic, talkative stretch, did you find yourself taking on more projects, spending money more freely, or doing things that were clearly out of character for you, even if others didn't comment on it directly?

Well, I did do one thing at work that wasn't really like me. I told a couple of vendors to just go ahead and hold some equipment for us, and I had them start the paperwork on it. But I did all that before I had really checked the budgets to see if we were cleared for it. Now I'm just... well, I'm worried I might have put us in a bad spot with the association's money.

target_item.manifestation: I told a couple of vendors to go ahead and hold equipment or start paperwork before I had really checked the budgets, and now I am worried I put us in a bad spot.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about taking on more projects, spending money freely, or doing things out of character, which aligns with excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences (such as telling vendors to hold equipment or start paperwork before checking budgets).

patient.answer: Well, I did do one thing at work that wasn't really like me. I told a couple of vendors to just go ahead and hold some equipment for us, and I had them start the paperwork on it. But I did all that before I had really checked the budgets to see if we were cleared for it. Now I'm just... well, I'm worried I might have put us in a bad spot with the association's money.

inference.note: The patient's report of impulsive, poorly judged financial/work decisions (committing to vendor equipment without budget clearance) during the elevated, talkative, irritable period adds functional consequences consistent with hypomania, and the episodic pattern with full inter-episode recovery argues against persistent MDD. This strengthens Bipolar II Disorder and effectively rules out F33.9.
